title: Microsoft Dataverse: management MCP server for building and governing MCP servers
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, commands and governance boundaries are supported. The changed advanced connector policies documentation still supports whole-server blocking rather than individual MCP-tool control. Minor corrections should finish the data-policy navigation path and cite the additional premium-connector licensing evidence.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: MCP tools can let agents read and write business data.
claims.quote:
search, read_query, and fetch – Enable copilots to dynamically locate, interpret, and respond using enterprise data.
create_record and update_record – Allow copilots to log new actions or modify existing records as part of conversational workflows.

claims.claim: Dataverse custom APIs can implement write actions.
claims.quote: An Action is an operation that makes changes to data in the system. It's invoked using the Http POST method and parameters are passed in the body of the request.

claims.claim: Consuming Copilot Studio agents may use Copilot Credits under their existing billing model.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.

claims.claim: Whether premium connectors need a licence depends on the consuming product and its licence.
claims.quote: If an instant flow has premium connectors, every user who runs the flow needs a Power Automate Premium license. In such cases, instead of licensing every user, you can license the flow with a Process license.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/faqs#how-do-power-automate-license-plans-work-for-flow-runs to sources for this general statement. The cited Copilot Studio billing page separately says its standalone subscription includes premium connectors.

claims.claim: Dataverse service protection limits constrain underlying Dataverse API use.
claims.quote: To ensure consistent availability and performance for everyone, Dataverse applies limits to how APIs are used. These limits detect when client applications make extraordinary demands on server resources.

claims.claim: The cited limits and consuming-agent billing do not establish a management-server quota or pricing meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse management MCP server licensing price prerequisites Copilot Credits; "management MCP server" "licensing" "price". Read api-limits, billing-licensing and mcp-management; none states a quota or meter for MCPManagement.

claims.claim: The environment availability setting is in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server.
claims.quote:
Select Manage > Environments.
Select the Environment Name ... select Settings. Under Settings, select Product > Features. ... locate Dataverse Model Context Protocol ... Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the Dataverse MCP availability switch is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse MCP server disable API organization settings IsMCPEnabled PowerShell pac admin; Dataverse MCP disable PowerShell; Power Platform REST MCP disable. Read configure, CLI and organization references; searched organization text for MCP. No switch-setting operation found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the Dataverse data-endpoint availability switch governs the management MCP endpoint.
claims.quote: Searched: management MCP server DLP access controls disable environment MCPManagement; Dataverse MCP server disable API organization settings. Read mcp-management, data-platform-mcp-disable and organization reference; no relationship between this switch and MCPManagement is stated.

claims.claim: Allowed clients are configured in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > client > Is Enabled.
claims.quote:
Select Advanced Settings.
The list of available clients is shown. Open the client record you want.
On the MCP client record, set Is Enabled to Yes.

claims.claim: dataverse mcp allow <appId> allows an application as a Dataverse MCP client for the current environment.
claims.quote:
Ensure that a Microsoft Entra application is in the Dataverse MCP allowed clients list for the current profile's environment.
dataverse mcp allow <appId> [options]
The <appId> argument is the application (client) ID to allow, as a GUID.

claims.claim: The preview Dataverse CLI allow command requires Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.
claims.quote:
This is a preview feature.
The authenticated user must have Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP client allow listing applies only to the /api/mcp agent entrypoint.
claims.quote: MCP allow listing applies only to the `/api/mcp` agent entrypoint. MCP‑named custom APIs are regular Dataverse APIs and aren't restricted by this setting.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center server block control is at Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab.
Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane.
Select Block to restrict the server across your organization, or Unblock to restore access to a previously blocked server.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the Microsoft 365 admin center MCP registry server/tool blocking control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Agent 365 MCP server block tools registry API; MCP block Graph API Agent 365. Read manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp; the CLI removed block. Graph Enterprise MCP and Azure gateway operations do not establish an equivalent registry blocking call.

claims.claim: The registered MCP-server Block action disables all its tools across the organization.
claims.quote:
Select Block to restrict the server across your organization ...
Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes. This action targets the server component, rather than a whole plugin package.

claims.claim: Individual tools are toggled in the selected registered MCP server's Tools tab.
claims.quote:
Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane.
Select the Tools tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an Enabled or Disabled toggle.
Turn individual tools on or off as needed.

claims.claim: Individual-tool control supports only specific registered MCP-server types.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces individual-tool policy for supported experiences using that gateway.
claims.quote: The Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces the policy at runtime for supported tools and experiences that use the gateway. Don't assume the policy applies across all products or connected components.

claims.claim: The registered-server controls are not shown to govern direct management-endpoint calls.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Agent 365 MCP server block tools registry API; management MCP server DLP access controls disable environment MCPManagement. Read mcp-management and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; gateway scope is stated, but direct MCPManagement enforcement is not.

claims.claim: Connector data policy configuration starts in Power Platform admin center at Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy.
claims.quote:
Select Security ... Data and privacy.
On the Data protection and privacy page, select Data policy.
Select ... New Policy ...
In the Prebuilt connectors section, select a Blockable connector ...
Select Configure connectors and then Connector actions.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct policy wizard but stops before connector configuration. Replace it with 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Configure connectors > Connector actions > Allow or Deny', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/connector-action-control.

claims.claim: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell provides New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy <policyDefinition> for creating a data policy from a definition.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module
Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object.
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy <Object>

claims.claim: Connector data policies cover MCP tools consumed by Copilot Studio agents in environments within the policy scope.
claims.quote:
These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.
Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: Classic connector data policies do not establish documented protection of direct management MCP endpoint calls.
claims.quote: Searched: management MCP server DLP access controls disable environment MCPManagement; "management MCP server" "DLP" "access". Read admin-data-loss-prevention, advanced-connector-policies and mcp-management; documented agent/connector scope does not identify direct management calls.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented management-MCP-specific governance configuration through an environment admin UI or API.
claims.quote: Searched: management MCP server DLP access controls disable environment MCPManagement; "management MCP" "controls" "admin". Read mcp-management, MCPServer and MCPTool references and develop-mcp. Server record ACLs and BYO permissions do not state management-endpoint governance configuration.

claims.claim: The management MCP Learn reference lists tools but does not describe the roadmap's DLP and server/tool access-control governance model.
claims.quote: Searched: "MCPManagement" "policy"; "management MCP server" "DLP" "access". Read the full mcp-management reference: preview notice, URL/scope and tool schemas; no DLP or server/tool governance procedure.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies can block an entire listed MCP server.
claims.quote: Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies do not offer granular control over individual MCP tools.
claims.quote: As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available. Blocking the entire MCP server is supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed advanced connector policy coverage of direct management endpoint calls.
claims.quote: Searched: advanced connector policies MCP server tools policies; management MCP server DLP access controls disable environment MCPManagement. Read advanced-connector-policies and mcp-management; listed-server enforcement is stated, not direct management-call enforcement.
